text: Games that are more fun on a second playthrough As the title says, have you found a game more enjoyable on a second playthrough? For me, most Metroidvanias I play are more enjoyable on a second playthrough because I know where everything is, so I can optimize my run to progress the way I want to. Nowhere is that more true than Silksong. I played the game on release, wanting to be as spoiler free as possible. However, the unexpected (and sometimes unfair) difficulty wore me down a lot. The learning process just wasn’t fun. On subsequent playthroughs, I now know what to expect and I know exactly where to go to play as much as I want with the crests and upgrades I want. It made the experience much more enjoyable to me (Bilewater still sucks though. Not because of the maggots, but because of the randomized enemy spawns that you can’t plan around).

text: I'm genuinely surprised Rewindead isn't getting more attention. It is a brilliant concept. I don't normally post but I feel compelled since the concept of this game is genuinely quite cool. It's like a speed runners dream. (The fella at the top of the leader board posts all his stuff online and it freaks me out how it is even possible) Lad you're a hitman who is looping in time. You start by killing a VIP, which sends you back in time. Now you need to take out yourself and the VIP. This repeats until you've finished every loop on the level. It's pretty simple at first, but the more loop they add, the wilder it gets. It's basically a puzzle shooter game at the end of the day. There is a whole ranking system, which forces you to actually play fast. It's pretty sneaky on how it baits you into optimising everything. You start thinking.... "NO I can't settle for a C! I am beyond a mere C! I will become number 1" but the faster you play, the harder the game gets (The past versions of you turn into a bit of a menace) I spent way too long trying to find the perfect run, just to find out some guy online to show me something I couldn't even imagine. TLDR: Gud Gam, Fun Gam, Try Demo
